# Conversion Patterns

Worked patterns for constructs that need more than a one-line mapping. The first four sections were moved from `copilot-instructions.md` and `@oracle-to-tsql`; the rest are new, each with sources. The T-SQL templates were run on SQL Server 2022.

## Hierarchical query (CONNECT BY → recursive CTE)

```sql
-- Oracle:
SELECT employee_id, manager_id, LEVEL
FROM employees
START WITH manager_id IS NULL
CONNECT BY PRIOR employee_id = manager_id;

-- T-SQL:
WITH EmployeeCTE AS (
    SELECT employee_id, manager_id, 1 AS level
    FROM dbo.employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT e.employee_id, e.manager_id, c.level + 1
    FROM dbo.employees e
    INNER JOIN EmployeeCTE c ON e.manager_id = c.employee_id
)
SELECT employee_id, manager_id, level
FROM EmployeeCTE
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 100);   -- set an appropriate limit
```

## Pagination (ROWNUM → OFFSET/FETCH)

```sql
-- Oracle:
SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT t.*, ROWNUM rn FROM (
        SELECT * FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC
    ) t WHERE ROWNUM <= 30
) WHERE rn > 20;

-- T-SQL:
SELECT * FROM dbo.employees
ORDER BY salary DESC
OFFSET 20 ROWS FETCH NEXT 10 ROWS ONLY;
```

## RETURNING INTO → OUTPUT

```sql
-- Oracle:
INSERT INTO employees (...) VALUES (...)
RETURNING employee_id INTO v_id;

-- T-SQL:
DECLARE @inserted TABLE (id BIGINT);
INSERT INTO dbo.employees (...)
OUTPUT inserted.employee_id INTO @inserted
VALUES (...);
SELECT @v_id = id FROM @inserted;
```

For a single-row insert into an `IDENTITY` table, `SET @v_id = SCOPE_IDENTITY();` also works. Avoid `@@IDENTITY`: it can return a value generated by a trigger. **Refs**: [SCOPE_IDENTITY](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/scope-identity-transact-sql)

## Dynamic SQL safety

```sql
-- Oracle:
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT * FROM ' || p_table_name;

-- T-SQL:
IF OBJECT_ID(@p_table_name, 'U') IS NULL
    THROW 50001, N'Table does not exist', 1;
DECLARE @sql NVARCHAR(4000) = N'SELECT * FROM ' + QUOTENAME(@p_table_name);
EXEC sp_executesql @sql;

-- Oracle: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT ...' INTO v_result USING p_param;
-- T-SQL:  EXEC sp_executesql N'SELECT @result = ...', N'@param INT, @result INT OUTPUT',
--                            @param = @p_param, @result = @v_result OUTPUT;
```

## Sequences

```sql
-- Oracle:  CREATE SEQUENCE my_seq START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1;
-- T-SQL:   CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.my_seq AS BIGINT START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1;

-- Oracle:  my_seq.NEXTVAL
-- T-SQL:   NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.my_seq

-- Oracle:  my_seq.CURRVAL
-- T-SQL:   no direct equivalent — capture NEXT VALUE FOR in a variable first
```

## Identity columns and sequence defaults

| Oracle | T-SQL | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `id NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` (12c+) | `id BIGINT IDENTITY(1,1)` | Both reject explicit values; data loads need `SET IDENTITY_INSERT dbo.t ON`. |
| `id NUMBER GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` | `CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.t_id_seq …;` + `id BIGINT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT df_t_id DEFAULT (NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.t_id_seq)` | Explicit values are allowed, as in Oracle. |
| `… GENERATED BY DEFAULT ON NULL AS IDENTITY` / `DEFAULT ON NULL expr` | Sequence default as above, plus `-- MIGRATION WARNING:` | ⚠️ SQL Server applies a default only when the column is omitted, not when `NULL` is inserted explicitly. Fix the callers or add an `INSTEAD OF INSERT` trigger. |
| `id NUMBER DEFAULT my_seq.NEXTVAL` (12c+) | `id BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT (NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.my_seq)` | |
| `BEFORE INSERT` trigger setting `:NEW.id := seq.NEXTVAL` (pre-12c) | Drop the trigger. Use `IDENTITY`, or a sequence default if the trigger had `WHEN (NEW.id IS NULL)` | A conditional trigger means callers could supply their own IDs. |

After loading data with explicit IDs, move the generator past the highest value: `DBCC CHECKIDENT (N'dbo.t', RESEED, <max_id>)` for `IDENTITY`, or `ALTER SEQUENCE dbo.t_id_seq RESTART WITH <max_id + 1>`.

```sql
-- Oracle (12c+)
CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id NUMBER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name        VARCHAR2(100) NOT NULL
);

-- T-SQL
CREATE TABLE dbo.customers (
    customer_id BIGINT IDENTITY(1,1) NOT NULL CONSTRAINT pk_customers PRIMARY KEY,
    name        NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);
```

**Refs**: [Oracle CREATE TABLE (identity_clause, DEFAULT ON NULL)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CREATE-TABLE.html) · [Oracle 12c new features (identity columns)](https://docs.oracle.com/database/121/NEWFT/chapter12101.htm) · [IDENTITY property](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-table-transact-sql-identity-property) · [NEXT VALUE FOR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/next-value-for-transact-sql) · [SET IDENTITY_INSERT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-identity-insert-transact-sql) · [DBCC CHECKIDENT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/database-console-commands/dbcc-checkident-transact-sql) · [ALTER SEQUENCE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-sequence-transact-sql) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — identity columns](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## MERGE

| Oracle | T-SQL |
|--------|-------|
| `WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET … WHERE cond` | `WHEN MATCHED AND cond THEN UPDATE SET …` |
| `… DELETE WHERE del_cond` (after `UPDATE`) | A separate `WHEN MATCHED AND cond AND <del_cond in terms of the new values> THEN DELETE`, placed **before** the `UPDATE` branch |
| `WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT … WHERE cond` | `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY TARGET AND cond THEN INSERT …` |
| Statement ends without `;` | Must end with `;` (error 10713 otherwise) |

- Oracle's `DELETE WHERE` only touches rows the `UPDATE` branch just updated, and evaluates the **updated** values. Rewrite the condition using the source values that the update assigns.
- Oracle can't update columns referenced in `ON`; SQL Server can. That's not a conversion problem, but don't add such updates.
- Both databases raise an error if one target row matches several source rows (SQL Server error 8672).
- SQL Server allows at most two `WHEN MATCHED` clauses, and one of them must be `DELETE` when there are two.
- `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE` has no Oracle counterpart — don't add it.

```sql
-- Oracle
MERGE INTO orders o
USING (SELECT order_id, invoice_status FROM fin_invoices) src
ON (o.order_id = src.order_id)
WHEN MATCHED THEN
    UPDATE SET o.status = src.invoice_status
    WHERE o.status <> 'CANCELLED'
    DELETE WHERE o.status = 'VOID';      -- evaluated on the updated row

-- T-SQL (verified)
MERGE dbo.orders AS o
USING (SELECT order_id, invoice_status FROM dbo.fin_invoices) AS src
    ON o.order_id = src.order_id
WHEN MATCHED AND o.status <> N'CANCELLED' AND src.invoice_status = N'VOID' THEN
    DELETE
WHEN MATCHED AND o.status <> N'CANCELLED' THEN
    UPDATE SET o.status = src.invoice_status;
```

**Refs**: [Oracle MERGE](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/MERGE.html) · [SQL Server MERGE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/merge-transact-sql) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — pitfall 4 (MERGE differences)](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## Transactions and error handling

See [semantic-differences §17](./semantic-differences.md#17-transactions-and-error-handling) for the behaviour behind these templates.

**Procedure that owns its transaction** (all-or-nothing — use when the application calls the procedure directly and treats any error as failure; verified that a failing second update rolls back the first):

```sql
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dbo.transfer_funds
    @from_id BIGINT, @to_id BIGINT, @amount DECIMAL(18,2)
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SET XACT_ABORT ON;                          -- any runtime error dooms the transaction
    DECLARE @own_tran BIT = 0;
    BEGIN TRY
        IF @@TRANCOUNT = 0 BEGIN BEGIN TRANSACTION; SET @own_tran = 1; END;

        UPDATE dbo.accounts SET balance = balance - @amount WHERE account_id = @from_id;
        UPDATE dbo.accounts SET balance = balance + @amount WHERE account_id = @to_id;

        IF @own_tran = 1 COMMIT TRANSACTION;
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        IF @own_tran = 1 AND XACT_STATE() <> 0 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;
        THROW;
    END CATCH
END;
```

**Called procedure whose Oracle caller handles the exception and carries on.** Oracle doesn't roll back a subprogram's earlier changes when it exits with an unhandled exception. Match that by leaving `XACT_ABORT` OFF in this call path and letting the error propagate (verified: the earlier update and the caller's work were kept; only the failing statement was undone):

```sql
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dbo.post_line @line_id BIGINT, @qty INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;                             -- XACT_ABORT stays OFF on purpose
    UPDATE dbo.lines SET posted = 1 WHERE line_id = @line_id;
    UPDATE dbo.lines SET qty = @qty WHERE line_id = @line_id;   -- if this fails, the first update stays
END;

-- Caller (was: BEGIN post_line(...); EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN log_error; END;)
BEGIN TRY
    EXEC dbo.post_line @line_id = @id, @qty = @qty;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
    IF XACT_STATE() = -1 ROLLBACK TRANSACTION;  -- MIGRATION WARNING: some errors doom the transaction in SQL Server
    -- log and continue, as the Oracle handler did
END CATCH;
```

| Oracle | T-SQL |
|--------|-------|
| `SAVEPOINT name` | `SAVE TRANSACTION name` (verified) |
| `ROLLBACK TO name` | `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION name` |

- An Oracle `COMMIT` inside a called procedure commits the caller's work too. In SQL Server it only decrements `@@TRANCOUNT` when nested. Flag every `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` inside called procedures with a `-- MIGRATION WARNING:`.

**Refs**: [SET XACT_ABORT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-xact-abort-transact-sql) · [XACT_STATE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/xact-state-transact-sql) · [SAVE TRANSACTION](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/save-transaction-transact-sql) · [COMMIT TRANSACTION](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/commit-transaction-transact-sql) · [Oracle — Unhandled exceptions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/lnpls/unhandled-exceptions.html) · [Oracle — Transactions](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/cncpt/transactions.html) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — pitfall 3 and best practice 3](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## Locking (SELECT … FOR UPDATE)

Oracle holds `FOR UPDATE` row locks until `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`. In SQL Server autocommit mode, locks from a standalone `SELECT` are released when the statement ends, so **always** wrap the locking read and the following DML in an explicit transaction.

| Oracle | T-SQL (inside `BEGIN TRANSACTION … COMMIT`) |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------|
| `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` | `SELECT … FROM dbo.t WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK) WHERE …` |
| `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` | `WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK, NOWAIT)` — fails at once with error 1222 if locked |
| `FOR UPDATE WAIT n` | `SET LOCK_TIMEOUT <n × 1000>;` before the `SELECT`, `SET LOCK_TIMEOUT -1;` after |
| `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` | `WITH (UPDLOCK, ROWLOCK, READPAST)` |
| `FOR UPDATE OF col` | Same hints; SQL Server locks rows, not columns |
| Cursor loop with `WHERE CURRENT OF` | One set-based `UPDATE` with the same hints, e.g. `UPDATE TOP (n) … WITH (ROWLOCK, READPAST)` for queues |

Never add `NOLOCK` — Oracle never reads uncommitted data. Prefer `READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON` so plain reads don't block ([semantic-differences §18](./semantic-differences.md#18-read-consistency-and-blocking)).

**Refs**: [Oracle SELECT (for_update_clause)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/SELECT.html) · [Table hints (UPDLOCK, READPAST, NOWAIT)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/queries/hints-transact-sql-table) · [SET LOCK_TIMEOUT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/set-lock-timeout-transact-sql) · [Transaction locking and row versioning guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/sql-server-transaction-locking-and-row-versioning-guide) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — best practice 6 (NOLOCK)](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## Schemas, database links and synonyms

| Oracle | T-SQL | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| Schema (= user) `hr` | `CREATE SCHEMA hr;` in one database | Keep two-part names: `hr.employees` → `[hr].[employees]`. |
| Separate Oracle databases | Separate SQL Server databases | Three-part names `[db].[schema].[table]` on the same instance. |
| `table@dblink` | `[LinkedServer].[Database].[Schema].[Table]` | Linked servers exist in SQL Server and Azure SQL Managed Instance, not Azure SQL Database. |
| Large filtered remote reads | `OPENQUERY(LinkedServer, 'SELECT … WHERE …')` | The query runs on the remote server. |
| DML over a link inside a transaction | Distributed transaction (MSDTC) | Oracle uses two-phase commit implicitly; SQL Server promotes to a distributed transaction. Test it. |
| `CREATE SYNONYM s FOR schema.obj[@dblink]` | `CREATE SYNONYM dbo.s FOR [Server].[Db].[Schema].[obj]` | SQL Server synonyms can point at linked-server objects. |
| `CREATE PUBLIC SYNONYM` | No equivalent | Synonyms belong to a schema; create one per schema that needs it, or use `dbo`. |

If a database link pointed at a database that's being consolidated into the same SQL Server instance, replace it with three-part names — no linked server needed.

**Refs**: [Oracle CREATE DATABASE LINK](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CREATE-DATABASE-LINK.html) · [Oracle CREATE SYNONYM](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CREATE-SYNONYM.html) · [Linked servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/linked-servers/linked-servers-database-engine) · [OPENQUERY](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/openquery-transact-sql) · [BEGIN DISTRIBUTED TRANSACTION](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/language-elements/begin-distributed-transaction-transact-sql) · [CREATE SYNONYM](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-synonym-transact-sql) · [CREATE SCHEMA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-schema-transact-sql) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — linked servers → database links, pitfall 5](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## Temporary tables

Oracle global temporary table (GTT) definitions are permanent and shared; each session sees only its own rows. SQL Server `#temp` tables are created at run time and dropped automatically.

| Oracle | T-SQL | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| `CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE … ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS` used inside one procedure | `CREATE TABLE #name (…)` at the start of that procedure | Dropped when the procedure ends. |
| GTT shared by several procedures in one session | `#temp` created by the outermost procedure (nested procedures can see it), or a memory-optimized `SCHEMA_ONLY` table filtered on `@@SPID` | The memory-optimized pattern is Microsoft's documented replacement for global temp tables. |
| `… ON COMMIT DELETE ROWS` | As above, plus `DELETE FROM #name` at each `COMMIT` point | No automatic equivalent; add a `-- MIGRATION NOTE:`. |
| `CREATE PRIVATE TEMPORARY TABLE ora$ptt_…` (18c+) | `CREATE TABLE #name (…)` | |

**Refs**: [Oracle CREATE TABLE (GLOBAL TEMPORARY, PRIVATE TEMPORARY)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/sqlrf/CREATE-TABLE.html) · [SQL Server CREATE TABLE (temporary tables)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-table-transact-sql) · [Faster temp tables with memory optimization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/in-memory-oltp/faster-temp-table-and-table-variable-by-using-memory-optimization) · Reversed from [oracle/skills — best practice 4 (tempdb usage)](https://github.com/oracle/skills/blob/main/db/migrations/migrate-sqlserver-to-oracle.md)

## Triggers

Oracle row triggers (`FOR EACH ROW`) fire once per affected row. SQL Server DML triggers fire **once per statement**, with all affected rows in the `inserted` and `deleted` tables. Every converted trigger must work for multi-row statements.

| Oracle | T-SQL |
|--------|-------|
| `FOR EACH ROW` | Set-based logic joining `inserted` / `deleted` on the primary key |
| `:NEW.col` / `:OLD.col` | `inserted.col` / `deleted.col` |
| `WHEN (NEW.status <> OLD.status)` | `WHERE i.status <> d.status` in the join (add NULL handling if the columns are nullable) |
| `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` that changes `:NEW` | Prefer a `DEFAULT`, computed column or constraint; otherwise an `INSTEAD OF` trigger that performs the DML with the computed values |
| `BEFORE INSERT` that assigns a sequence | Drop it; see [Identity columns and sequence defaults](#identity-columns-and-sequence-defaults) |
| `INSERTING` / `UPDATING` / `DELETING` | `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inserted)` / `deleted` combinations |
| `UPDATING('col')` / `AFTER UPDATE OF col` | `IF UPDATE(col)` |
| Statement-level trigger | Plain trigger |
| Compound triggers and mutating-table workarounds | Query the table directly — SQL Server has no mutating-table error |

```sql
-- Oracle
CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER trg_orders_status
AFTER UPDATE OF status ON orders
FOR EACH ROW
WHEN (NEW.status <> OLD.status)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO order_audit (order_id, old_status, new_status)
    VALUES (:OLD.order_id, :OLD.status, :NEW.status);
END;

-- T-SQL (verified with a multi-row UPDATE)
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER dbo.trg_orders_status
ON dbo.orders
AFTER UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    IF NOT UPDATE(status) RETURN;
    INSERT INTO dbo.order_audit (order_id, old_status, new_status)
    SELECT d.order_id, d.status, i.status
    FROM inserted AS i
    JOIN deleted  AS d ON d.order_id = i.order_id
    WHERE i.status <> d.status;
END;
```

**Refs**: [Oracle CREATE TRIGGER (FOR EACH ROW, BEFORE)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/lnpls/CREATE-TRIGGER-statement.html) · [SQL Server CREATE TRIGGER](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/create-trigger-transact-sql) · [Use the inserted and deleted tables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/triggers/use-the-inserted-and-deleted-tables) · [UPDATE() trigger function](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/update-trigger-functions-transact-sql)
